_how: One entry per ticket iid, labelled by a person who has read the ticket and the kept test-case list in state/runs/<iid>/testcases-eval.json. project: the ticket's GitLab project URL. runId: the record's runId — labels are only graded against that run. requirements: each labelled id's requirement text as it read when labelled; ids are positional and re-minted every run, so a reworded or vanished requirement is refused rather than regraded. real: each judge requirement id that IS a requirement, mapped to the case id in the kept list that truly covers it, or null when no case does. A case covers a requirement when it executes and asserts the substance — a residual hop is a finding, not a coverage error — and a case that cannot execute covers nothing. notReal: judge requirement ids that are not requirements. missed: one line per real requirement the judge never listed. A requirement the judge RETIRED is scored apart: in notReal it is credit, in real it counts against recall, and neither enters the precision denominator. why: free prose, read by nothing. Run `npm run eval:gold`.

requirements.R1: When a recreational-trip expense is Reimbursed, each active non-subcontractor participant's ExpensePerson.amount must equal amount_paid divided equally by the number of such participants.
requirements.R2: The sum of active participants' ExpensePerson.amount for a Reimbursed trip must equal (not exceed) amount_paid, and amount_paid itself must stay unchanged.
requirements.R3: Deciding an expense as Reimbursed must recompute and overwrite ExpensePerson.amount from the officer's entered amount_paid rather than leaving the creation-time figure in place.
requirements.R4: Submitting a multi-participant claim must create exactly one ExpensePerson row per participant, with no inactive duplicate rows.
requirements.R5: A global-subcontractor participant must be recorded at 0 and excluded from the equal-division divisor, so eligible participants absorb the full pot.
requirements.R6: A non-subcontractor participant who has already used part of their annual recreational-trip entitlement must still receive an equal share at decision time, not be silently assigned 0 while co-participants absorb it.
requirements.R7: Saving Amount Paid while a trip claim is still In-Progress (before any Reimbursed decision) must not rewrite ExpensePerson.amount.

missed: The apportionment must fire only on Travel / Recreational Trip claims: an Official Trip claim's ExpensePerson.amount and a non-travel expense type must come out of a Reimbursed decision unchanged. The kept list tests this (TC-18, TC-11) but no judge requirement states it, so dropping those cases would not have been caught.
8781.why: Travel Expense Claim Division Error, a dry drive — the record is state-dry/state/runs/8781/testcases-eval.json, so grade it with `DRY_RUN=1 npm run eval:gold -- 8781`; plain eval:gold reads state/runs, where run r-mupd17hc-d92b6b never ran the evaluation. R1-R5 are comment 4's oracle and the repro verbatim (amount_paid / participant count, sum == amount_paid, propagate at the decision, one row per participant, subcontractor at 0 and out of the divisor), and each maps to a kept case that drives the real Reimbursed decision and asserts the figure to the cent. R6 is real though the ticket never spells it out: equal division by head count is exactly what must stop a partly-used entitlement reducing a share, and it is the regression guard against the old parts weighting that caused the bug — TC-21 builds P4 with remaining entitlement below the equal share and holds every row at 11,000. R7 is not a requirement: the ticket asks only that the officer's figure reach the rows, never that the write be deferred until the decision. That deferral is the plan's own design (TC-04's oracle says outright that the ticket is silent on the provisional claim-time figure), so a fix that apportioned on save would satisfy every ticket requirement and still fail R7 — the judge promoted an implementation detail it read in the code. AC6 (review Limit 49,000 vs 92,000) and AC7 (admin In-Progress vs dashboard Pending) are NOT labelled missed: comment 4 lists both as unconfirmed by the reporter, so neither is a requirement the list owed a case.

requirements.R1: Every Amount cell on Payroll > People Report renders with at most two decimal places.
requirements.R2: Thousands separators appear only in the integer part of an Amount, never inside the decimal part, so the ticket's three API values render as 145,635.26, 78.00 and 1,460,414.86.
requirements.R3: The shared convertToNumberWithCommas helper must stop applying the thousands-separator regex to the decimal part, so every call site of the helper loses the comma-in-decimals defect.
requirements.R4: A People Report amount is rounded to two decimals rather than truncated, so 145635.25999999998 shows .26 and not .25.
requirements.R5: get_person_long_term_benefit_amount rounds the PF/gratuity sum to two decimals, so the People Report API no longer emits amounts with long decimal tails.
requirements.R6: Call sites that pass no fractionDigits argument keep the digits they displayed before, with no padding or truncation to two decimals.
requirements.R7: A non-numeric placeholder passed to the formatter, such as the '-' used for a missing provident fund figure, still passes through unchanged.
requirements.R8: A People Report amount of exactly zero renders with two decimals as '0.00'.
requirements.R9: The People Report CSV export's Amount column carries at most two decimal places, since the export writes the same rounded helper value.

missed: One named person's Amount must read the same on the People Report screen, in the data the page fetched for that row, and in the exported file — the whole point of rounding once on the server. anosha.saeed demanded exactly this on 2026-09-30; the judge instead split the surfaces into three independent requirements (R1 screen, R5 API, R9 CSV) and never stated the agreement between them, so nothing would notice if the screen and the export disagreed for the same person.
8772.why: Payroll People Report, commas inside the decimals — record state-dry/state/runs/8772/testcases-eval.json, graded with `DRY_RUN=1 npm run eval:gold -- 8772`. Drive ended on error_max_turns at eval lap 2, so final.status is fail/eval-error; chosenAttempt 1 is intact and is what these labels judge. All 9 requirements are real, which is the honest reading: R1/R2/R4 are the ticket's Summary, Expected table and 'Round to 2 decimals' verbatim; R3 is its Root cause section; R5 is its 'Optionally round the amount in the backend too', which the approved plan adopted; R8 settles the trailing-zero open question the plan explicitly decided; R6 is the plan's own opt-in boundary (a global 2-dp default 'silently turns 1,234.5 into 1,234.50 on 19 screens nobody asked about'), so not padding the other ~20 call sites is a requirement of the chosen approach, not an invention; R7 guards the formatter's existing non-numeric passthrough at misc.js:536, which arsal.tariq raised as the 'PKR -' placeholder. Two coverage calls are worth reading closely. R6 I map to TC-15, not the judge's TC-21: R6 forbids BOTH padding and truncation, and TC-21 only injects long decimals (proving no truncation) while TC-15 is the case that asserts a raw 1234.5 still reads '1,234.5' and that no decimal digits are added or removed. R7 I leave at TC-14, agreeing with the judge, even though the judge's own open finding F1 says TC-14 is the only case reaching that branch and is gated BLOCKED on two unrelated conditions — a case that asserts the behaviour still covers it, and counting F1 as a coverage error too would charge the judge twice for one problem. Flip R7 to null if you read a conditionally-blocked case as no cover.

requirements.R1: The dashboard shows exactly one row per team and month, with no duplicate team/month pairs, across January 2026 through the previous month.
requirements.R2: The listed month window starts at January 2026 and ends at the month before the current one, including correct rollback across a year boundary.
requirements.R3: A team and month whose logs are all submitted and approved must not appear as a row.
requirements.R4: A subteam with default_log_approved set whose weeks are all submitted must not appear, because approval is not required for it.
requirements.R5: A team/month is pending when a log is unsubmitted, or submitted-but-unapproved on a subteam that does not have default_log_approved.
requirements.R6: A pending log is attributed to the month of its week_starting date, including weeks that straddle two months.
requirements.R7: Each row displays the team name, its approver(s), the month, and the last escalation timestamp (empty when never escalated).
requirements.R8: The approvers shown for a row are the approvers of that team for that month.
requirements.R9: Rows can be selected individually or all at once, and only checked rows are escalated (send is unavailable with nothing selected).
requirements.R10: Expanding a row lists the people with pending logs for that team and month.
requirements.R11: Each pending person appears once with a deterministic reason of either not submitted or submitted-not-approved.
requirements.R12: Sending an escalation sends one email per log approver of the team, addressed to that approver by name.
requirements.R13: The configured escalation CC address (rizwan.aslam@arbisoft.com) is placed in CC of each escalation email when CC is requested.
requirements.R14: The email subject is exactly the specified mail-merge line naming the team, with no unresolved placeholders.
requirements.R15: The email body reuses the specified reminder copy with the signature overridden to Finance Team, Arbisoft.
requirements.R16: The last escalation timestamp is persisted per team/month and is still shown after a page reload.
requirements.R17: The last escalation timestamp is stamped only when at least one email for that team/month actually succeeded.
requirements.R18: All three escalation endpoints reject a user without the Finance escalation permission with 403.
requirements.R19: The dashboard route is gated on the escalation permission flag so a non-permitted user never renders it.
requirements.R20: The person payload exposes is_project_logs_escalation_reviewer so the UI can gate the route and sidebar entry.
requirements.R22: The existing automated first reminder to employees continues to work unchanged.
requirements.R24: A month outside the January 2026 to previous-month window is rejected by the API rather than escalated.
requirements.R25: A team/month with no log approver sends no email and is reported back as not sent with a reason.
requirements.R26: Only subteams under a team with an active contract for that month are listed, evaluated month by month.
requirements.R27: The listing endpoint's query count scales with the month range, not with the number of pending logs or people.

missed: AC14: the automated Day-5 / Day-7 approver reminder emails must no longer be sent automatically, because the dashboard replaces them. No requirement states it, and TC-27 asserts the opposite — that the legacy approver reminder still fires and still emails approvers — so the list would pass a build that kept the automatic reminders the ticket asked to retire.

AC12: the dashboard must be readable in dark theme. TC-26 measures WCAG 2.1 AA contrast on the dark render, but no judge requirement mentions theme or contrast, so dropping TC-26 would not have been caught.
8344.why: Pending Project Logs Escalation Dashboard for Finance — record state-dry/state/runs/8344/testcases-eval.json, graded with `DRY_RUN=1 npm run eval:gold -- 8344`. One attempt only: the list-regeneration lap died of an infrastructure stall (no stream message for 15m), so final is fail/testcases-failed with chosenAttempt 0, which these labels judge. All 25 listed requirements are real. The code-sourced ones earn it: R6's week_starting attribution is the rule that decides whether a Dec-29 week exists at all under AC2's January floor, R26's per-month contract gate silently decides which teams Finance can escalate, and R27 is the repo's own no-N+1 rule on a new teams x months x people listing. I verified the judge's critical finding F1 against the branch before labelling, and it is half right: send_project_logs_escalation(team_months, cc_advisory_admin) at pending_logs_escalation.py:219 really does take no requester, so TC-21, TC-22 and TC-27 do raise TypeError as written — but F1 also names TC-03, TC-13, TC-14 and TC-19, and none of those passes requester (TC-19 posts to the HTTP endpoint, the other three drive the UI dialog), so they execute fine. That is why only R12 is a false cover: its one real cover, TC-21, is the per-approver salutation case that cannot run, and TC-03 proves only that a single approver gets a mail, not one-per-approver-by-name. R17 moves to TC-14, which is executable and asserts stamping in both directions (S9 stamped, S8 not), rather than the dead TC-22. Five coverage calls name the wrong case rather than overclaiming, and two of them look like a straight swap: R10 (expanding a row lists pending people) is TC-02, not the 403 case TC-08, while R18 (three endpoints return 403) is TC-08, not the 400-validation case TC-10 — and TC-10's own field-scoped-400 behaviour has no requirement at all. R19 is TC-09, the new route's Not Found page, not TC-17, which exists to prove the PermissionGuard rewrite did not break the pre-existing TeamChecklist forbidden page. R5 is TC-18, the only case that branches the pending predicate on default_log_approved in both directions; the judge's TC-02 tests the expanded list, which is R10's job. R3, R8, R14, R15 and R22 are genuinely uncovered and the judge said so: nothing varies an approver across months (R8), nothing asserts the exact subject line or the 'Finance Team, Arbisoft' signature override from AC8/AC9 (R14, R15), and TC-27 exercises the approver-reminder command, not notify_person_project_logs, so it does not cover R22. Two things to note beyond the grade: the judge's own numbering skips R21 and R23 with dropped and retired both empty, which is unexplained; and AC7 reads as an unconditional CC to the configured address while R13 and TC-11 both encode an opt-in that defaults OFF — if the plan did not consciously amend AC7, R13 is wrong rather than merely narrow.

requirements.R1: Accounts can create a FixedBillingSalaryRecord by hand from the Django admin add form, with the six pipeline fields (invoice amount paid, percentage applied, salary amount, invoice, invoice sent date, salary payment date) editable rather than locked.
requirements.R2: Change (edit) access to existing FixedBillingSalaryRecord rows is withdrawn from all users while add access remains.
requirements.R3: A Django management command (not a PeriodicTask row) sends one reminder email per active fixed-billing subcontractor who has incomplete work logs, listing the projects concerned.
requirements.R4: The reminder email body matches the text given in the ticket verbatim, interpolating the person name and the project name(s).
requirements.R5: The reminder is scoped to the PREVIOUS month's logs and to people who held the fixed-billing employment type in that month, and is an early-in-the-month send.
requirements.R6: The People report and the Deel Salary People report show the latest FixedBillingSalaryRecord salary for people on the Subcontractor Fixed Billing employment type instead of the regular salary+increment figure.
requirements.R7: Zero is a displayable answer: a fixed-billing person with no active record for the target month shows 0 rather than an older month's amount or a non-fixed-billing salary figure.
requirements.R8: A salary_month entered on the admin form is normalised to the first of that month so it matches the unique_together key and every pipeline lookup.
requirements.R9: A person carrying no employment_type is treated as not fixed-billing and does not raise, so report exports and the reminder audience query stay safe.
requirements.R11: A mid-month salary_month that normalises onto an existing (person, team, month) row is rejected as a form validation error rather than a database IntegrityError.

missed: The fixed-billing substitution must stay confined to the two report surfaces: the general-purpose salary functions must keep returning the regular salary+increments figure for a fixed-billing person, so payslips and every other consumer are unaffected. TC-34 asserts exactly this and no requirement states it, so dropping that case would not have been caught — and AC6 names only the two reports, which makes the containment the boundary of the whole change.

The Bonus & Increment Year export is a third surface carrying the same Current Salary figure, and it must show the fixed-billing total (TC-37) and zero where no record exists (TC-38). R6 names only the People and Deel Salary People reports, so neither case is anchored to a requirement.
8792.why: Subcontractor Fixed Billing ver2 — record state-dry/state/runs/8792/testcases-eval.json, graded with `DRY_RUN=1 npm run eval:gold -- 8792`. The only drive that ran the loop to completion: three judge laps, two regenerations, all ok, stopped on retry-limit with coverage climbing 3/9 to 9/9, so chosenAttempt 2 (32 cases) is a genuinely matured list. Eight of nine coverage calls I agree with, and they are well grounded: TC-03 normalises a mid-month salary_month to the first (R8), TC-07 takes the unique_together collision as a form error rather than an IntegrityError (R11), TC-23 checks the seeded template word for word with both placeholders intact (R4), TC-25 scopes the audience to the previous month (R5), TC-31 makes zero a displayed answer (R7), TC-32 keeps a null employment_type on the regular path without raising (R9). One disagreement: R6 says the People AND Deel Salary People reports show the fixed-billing figure, and the judge maps it to TC-29, which checks only the two exports; TC-28 is the case that checks the on-screen Current salary column, which is where a reader of R6 would look first, so I map R6 to TC-28 and treat TC-29 as the export half. R3 I leave at TC-21 and agree, deliberately unlike 8344's R12: the open finding F1 is right that every command case patches the Celery task out so notify_fixed_billing_persons_project_logs_fill is never actually called, but TC-21 does execute and does assert the audience and the per-person payload, which is R3's substance. The rule I have applied across all four tickets: a case covers a requirement when it executes and asserts the substance, a residual hop is a finding; a case that cannot execute at all (8344's TC-21, dead on a requester argument the signature does not take) covers nothing. R2 is the interesting one and I have labelled it notReal, agreeing with the judge's own RET-R2 retirement: comment 1 reads 'just remove read only fields for admin table, we remove edit table permissions for all users', where 'just' scopes the code change to the read-only fields and the permission withdrawal is something the team does in admin groups, and the diff adds no has_change_permission override. Note this scores backwards. gradeAgainstGold builds `listed` from requirements PLUS retired, so a retired id labelled notReal still counts against precision — the judge is penalised for having reached the same conclusion I did, and labelling R2 real would have rewarded it for withdrawing a requirement I call genuine. The grader has no bucket for a correct retirement. Also unexplained, as on 8344: the numbering skips R10 with dropped empty on every attempt.
